Data sources

Fluxes are volumes of packed sand (pore space included) per metre width per year of 365.25 days (m²/yr). Drift potentials, crest fluxes and dune-orientation modes follow the methods reviewed in Courrech du Pont et al. (2024).
  • Dune map: dune-mask-rev1.tif from the Supplementary Code record (Zenodo, MIT), vectorised into dune fields.
  • Saturated flux divergence ${mathHtml("$\\nabla\\cdot\\vec{q}_s$")}: divergence of the time-averaged saturated sand-flux vector (magnitude RDP, direction RDD) on the sphere, ∇·q = [∂(q cos θ)/∂λ + ∂(q sin θ cos φ)/∂φ] / (R cos φ) with q = RDP, θ = RDD, latitude φ, longitude λ and R = 6371 km, computed with central differences on the grid of the selected wind dataset (${datasetFacts("resolution")}), following Gunn (2026), Methods M6. By conservation of sand mass, negative values (convergence) imply deposition and positive values erosion, in metres of bed level per thousand years.
